clock._comment: Task 1.13. The dashboard clock's starting state. Union calendar of 365 days (D15); Basin year = Union year - 5017, so 5029u is Basin year 12. Orbit phases are given at the epoch, 5029u day 1. The Lantern tide runs 73 days, open on cycle days 1-14 (D7); on day 300 it is on cycle day 5, so tidal lanes are open for 9 more days. Late 5029u fits the sources: the drone came through about four months earlier, and Kasprzak was last seen in early summer.

factions.name: Charter folk
factions.notes: About 340,000 people crossed with the Charter fleet, as crew or as colonists in cold storage. They brought the Third Committee's Union with them and its habits: civic duty, careful records and a faith in institutions that the Lean Years tested hard. Charter families staff most of the Bench and much of the Navy's older officer corps. The courier drone has shaken them more than anyone; some have stopped filing claims, on the grounds that they may not be staying.

factions.name: The tail
factions.notes: Roughly nine hundred thousand people crossed on permits or without them: free companies, prospectors, religious communities, Cosmopolitan crews and private colony ventures. They share a habit of looking after themselves and a long memory of the Requisition. Tail families run most of the Basin's independent trade and crew most of its free companies, and many still keep their Requisition receipts.

factions.name: The Thawed
factions.notes: More than a hundred thousand colonists woken from cold storage since the Closing, about four thousand more each year. Most expected to wake on a settled garden world and woke to a Basin at war, the best land taken and families split between the waking and the sleeping. They make up a large part of the Stacks and of the Compact, and the thaw lists anger them more than anything else.

factions.name: The Basin-born
factions.notes: About a fifth of the people in the Basin, none older than twelve. They have never used the omninet or seen a blink gate, speak a mix of fleet jargon and tail dialects, and take drifting lanes, lattice and custodians for granted. The Stewardship, the Purview and the Synod each run schools that teach a different account of the Closing.

factions.name: Seam crews
factions.notes: The miners who work lattice on Scald, on Gloam's night side and in the Shoals, drawn from every other group. The work pays well and kills many of them. Seam crews keep their own company and customs, distrust anyone who has never worked deep, and are superstitious about the custodians. The Listeners came out of their ranks.

bodies.notes: Tidally locked to a dim red star, with one face in permanent day and the other in permanent night. The day side is a dry, wind-scoured desert under a sun that never moves. places.notes: Headquarters of the Bench's Survey Office, about two thousand scientists, survey crews and guards.

places.name: Basin Office headquarters
places.notes: Director Hannelore Sato's offices. The IPS-N Basin Office keeps its legal title, its contracts and its yards, and still claims the Free Lines' ships.

places.name: The lower decks
places.notes: The deepest levels of the Stacks. In 5026u marines in frames killed 212 people clearing them after a leaked thaw list set off three days of riots.

places.name: Gallowglass berth
places.notes: Where Gallowglass keeps its boarding craft between contracts.

places.name: Synod chapel (WIP)
places.notes: A Wayfarer Synod congregation's chapel in the Stacks.

places.name: Ostrom Standard works (WIP)
places.notes: Print halls where Ostrom Standard turns out cheap, sturdy GMS-pattern frames for Navy auxiliaries and the Landholders' League.

places.name: Waymeet (WIP)
places.notes: Seat of the Wayfarer Synod's council of elders, at the head of a northern fjord.

places.name: Northern landing grounds
places.notes: The Synod's landing fields. In 5027u Synod and Navy ships exchanged fire over them, and the Navy lost two landing craft.

places.name: The southern ring
places.notes: Pennant's largest Absent climate structure: a ring of bare rock about forty kilometers across where nothing grows and snow never settles.

places.name: Corvel landing

control.note: Under siege by the Pilgrim Guard

places.notes: Six hundred hired frames, most of them Lantern Company's, landed by Corvel in 5028u to hold its claim. The Synod's Pilgrim Guard destroyed their dropships early in 5029u and has kept them under siege since.

places.name: Hearthfjord (WIP)
places.notes: Second town of the Synod's north, a timber and fishing port at the head of a deep fjord.

places.name: Guardhold (WIP)
places.notes: Fortress and training ground of the Pilgrim Guard, which flies Smith-Shimano frames bought over a decade of careful saving.

places.name: Rootwater (WIP)
places.notes: Gardener farmsteads on the southern coast of the northern continent.

places.name: Reachward yards (WIP)
places.notes: Where the Synod is gathering ships, colonists and prefab for its own settlement of the Lantern Reach.

places.name: Burned camp
places.notes: The Corvel survey camp burned in 5028u, which led Corvel to land six hundred hired frames.

places.name: Southern picket (WIP)
places.notes: Pilgrim Guard picket keeping the Corvel landing cut off from resupply.

places.name: Siege lines
places.notes: The Pilgrim Guard's lines around the Corvel landing.

places.name: Tew II open pits (WIP)
places.notes: Open-pit metal workings on the night side of Tew II.

places.name: Brokers' Row (WIP)
places.notes: The market where Registry-banned designs and levy-free lattice change hands openly.

places.name: Harbormasters' hall (WIP)
places.notes: Where the loose council of harbormasters, brokers and captains meets.

places.name: Tally berth (WIP)
places.notes: Berths the harbormasters do not acknowledge, where Tallymen crews dock and sell what they take.

places.name: Kettle Flats
places.notes: The Haldane family's claims, center of the Northern Concord. The fighting here in 5028u cost about 140 frames in four days and moved the line less than ten kilometers.

places.name: The Seam
places.notes: A six-hundred-kilometer front across open glass between the Northern Concord and the Southern League. Thirty or forty free companies are under contract on Scald at any one time.

places.name: Kerrtown
places.notes: Kerr-Varga's company town on the southern edge of the glassfields, where it builds frames around lattice reactors. Defended by a works militia of some six thousand.

places.name: Kerrtown refinery
places.notes: Kerr-Varga refinery attacked by a group of Listeners in 5028u.

places.name: Syndicate registry
places.notes: Where ARBITRAGE keeps a single registry of glassfield claims for both halves of the Syndicate. Each half has tried at least once to steal its core.

places.name: Purview expeditionary camp (WIP)
places.notes: Base of the two thousand Purview troops under Major-General Ines Duroc fighting for the Southern League, supplied through the Halvard Gap.

places.name: Listener wells (WIP)
places.notes: A Listener community among the deep extraction sites of the unglassed highlands.

places.name: Haldane House (WIP)
places.notes: Seat of the Haldane family, whose claims around Kettle Flats lead the Northern Concord.

places.name: League hall (WIP)
places.notes: Meeting place of the Southern League's claim-holders under Tomas Recaldo.

places.name: Navy lease camp (WIP)
places.notes: Camp of the dozen Navy frame companies leased to the Northern Concord.

places.name: Saltmarsh line (WIP)
places.notes: The stretch of the Concord's front held by Saltmarsh, thinned since two hundred frames were pulled back to the Marrow.

places.name: Dunmore Rifles camp (WIP)
places.notes: Base of the largest company on the Southern League's line, flying Armory designs.

places.name: Glasstown (WIP)
places.notes: Claims town on the northern glass, built of glass blocks cut from the fields.

places.name: Deep site fourteen (WIP)
places.notes: The fourteenth deep extraction site attacked by custodians below four hundred meters.

places.name: Sabotaged extraction site (WIP)
places.notes: A deep extraction site wrecked by a Listener community.

places.name: Firstbreath (WIP)
places.notes: Largest of Bellows's sealed towns, where the Commune's council meets.

places.name: Sealhold (WIP)
places.notes: A sealed mining town working shallow lattice in the closed season.

places.name: Swash claim camp (WIP)
places.notes: Independent claim crews working shallow seams that a single crew can mine.

places.name: The Landing
places.notes: First settlement on Tallis, put down on the east coast in 5017u. Its first winter killed about a third of the settlers. In 5019u Ivo Halloran seized its grain stores for nine days.

places.name: Tallis garrison
places.notes: Commodore Isaac Ferrante's command. Sweeps the Reach every dry season.
places._comment: Location near the Landing is invented.

places.name: Dry Creek
places.notes: Nineteen people died here in 5027u, six of them veterans, in a land dispute between Compact farmers and Navy veterans. The Reach went to war.

places.name: Sallow Ford
places.notes: The Compact held the town for eleven weeks in 5028u. CARILLON refused to direct the Severn's guns against it, and Ferrante retook it with ground artillery. Several hundred civilians died; Command suspended the Bench's inquiry.

places.name: Weirmouth (WIP)
places.notes: River port at the mouth of the largest of the eastern valleys, where Combine barges meet coastal shipping.

places.name: Fallowfield (WIP)
places.notes: Headquarters of the Riverlands Combine and its largest granaries. Grain leaves here under Navy guard for the Marrow and the inner Basin.

places.name: Veterans' Rest (WIP)
places.notes: Market town of the Tallis Landholders' League on the edge of the Reach, where the League musters its frame lances. Commodore Ferrante speaks at its meetings.

places.name: Dustwater (WIP)
places.notes: Compact district center in the Reach, farmed without title since the early thaw years.

places.name: Saltbrush (WIP)
places.notes: Compact district in the dry south of the Reach, where the rains fail most years.

places.name: Greenhold (WIP)
places.notes: A Gardeners' farming community that has refused lattice-built machinery for a decade.

places.name: Eastshore airfield (WIP)
places.notes: Navy airfield and frame depot supporting the garrison's dry-season sweeps of the Reach.

places.name: Survey shaft (WIP)
places.notes: Survey Office shaft sunk several kilometers toward one of the eleven climate structures, the first found in 5021u.

places.name: Farshore (WIP)
places.notes: Frontier homesteads on the smaller continent, filed under the Allotment and thinly governed.

places.name: Landing chapel of the Vigil (WIP)
places.notes: The Vigil of the Open Door's chapel at the Landing, crowded since the drone came through.

places.name: Survey base camp (WIP)
places.notes: Basin Office ground camp beneath the rings.

places.name: Ice-core camp (WIP)
places.notes: Survey camp drilling through Lethe's frozen ocean toward the remains of the life beneath.

places.name: Anchorhold (WIP)
places.notes: The largest of the lagoon towns this season, and so the meeting place of the Moorage.

places.name: Brinemoor (WIP)
places.notes: A lagoon town of repair yards and hostels serving ships at anchor.

places.name: Longfall (WIP)
places.notes: The Long Families' home anchorage, where their convoy stops when it stops for long.

places.name: Tidewrack (WIP)
places.notes: Lagoon town of net-makers and sea farmers.

places.name: Highwater (WIP)
places.notes: Lagoon town moored in the deepest lagoon, the only one that never grounds at low tide.

places.name: Kelpmoor (WIP)
places.notes: Lagoon town harvesting the kelp beds of the southern islands.

places.name: Reedhaven (WIP)
places.notes: Small lagoon town known for its hostels and its discretion.

places.name: Envoys' Quay (WIP)
places.notes: Moorings where the Stewardship, the Synod and the Free Lines keep their agents.

places.name: Burned copy-house (WIP)
places.notes: The Long Families copy-house burned out by the Ninefold on Corvel's contract in 5028u. Three of the Families' people died in the fire, and the chart war began.

places.name: Harbor guard moorings (WIP)
places.notes: Home of the towns' only armed force, a harbor guard of armed boats.

places.name: The pupil shore (WIP)
places.notes: The edge of Iris's single open ocean, where survey crews have found microbial mats.

areas.notes: The habitable strip between day and night, settled by the Purview.

areas.name: Twilight band (west)
areas.notes: The habitable strip between day and night, settled by the Purview.

areas.name: Night side (east)
areas.notes: Frozen night side, rich in lattice. Purview troops are clearing the Coldwell camps one at a time.

areas.name: Night side (west)
areas.notes: Frozen night side, rich in lattice.

areas.name: Northern continent
areas.notes: Fjords and broad river valleys; nearly all of Pennant's settlements.

areas.name: Southern continent

control.note: Corvel's claim, besieged by the Synod

areas.notes: Wild and largely empty. Corvel surveyed it in 5026u and filed claims on nearly all of it.

areas.name: Concord glassfields
areas.notes: Glassfields north of the Seam, held by the Northern Concord with leased Navy frame companies and Saltmarsh.

areas.name: League glassfields
areas.notes: Glassfields south of the Seam, held by the Southern League with Kerr-Varga, Dunmore Rifles and the Purview.

areas.name: River valleys and east coast
areas.notes: Governed directly by the Stewardship. The best farmland in the Basin; the Riverlands Combine farms it and feeds the inner Basin.

areas.name: The Reach
areas.notes: High, dry interior upland. Governed on paper through appointed councils, most of which the Compact ignores. About twelve thousand Compact militia; the Landholders' League patrols its edge.
